rationale: Banned tolokers are workers gaming tasks, not structurally exotic accounts: the platform's ban criterion is behavioural (bad or automated task performance) while the graph edges only say 'worked on the same task', so co-work structure is largely task-scheduling noise, not a fraud signal. That mismatch is visible in the profile: density 0.015 with avg_degree 88 and clustering 0.533 means neighbourhoods are huge, overlapping project cliques, so neighbour-averaging views are diluted; the density landmarker is degenerate (p90 = p95 = 0.0, mean 0.0023), which rules out embedding-space sparsity, and spectral is flat (p95 0.416, no separated tail), so high-frequency structural views have nothing to find. Feature-space views carry the signal instead. feature_dup_rate 0.489 with only feature_dim 10 and feature_sparsity 0.48 means the profile/performance matrix is template-dominated: banned workers hide behind minimal or default profile statistics rather than standing out, which is exactly camouflage-by-conformity, and its landmarker is the dominant one (mean 0.811, p50 0.870) with a dense high-conformity mass to rank within. attr_struct_mismatch has the most separated upper tail of the discriminative landmarkers (p50 0.314 to p99 0.914, std 0.245): a worker whose profile statistics disagree with the projects they are embedded in is the practitioner's real suspicion. one_class adds a genuinely complementary global view: with 26 communities at modularity 0.519, banned behaviour is a deviation from the single global 'legitimate worker' performance profile, not from any one project, and SVDD in a 10-dimensional attribute space is well conditioned here. local_affinity is included last as a mild homophily check (homophily 0.749) to catch workers who are anomalous relative to their own project peers; community and homophily_violation are dropped as redundant with it and with attr_struct_mismatch, and reconstruction is dropped because on a template-dominated matrix its residual is the sign-inverted twin of conformity.

Banned tolokers are cheaters who game tasks, and cheating profiles are deliberately unremarkable: the feature matrix is template-dominated (feature_dup_rate = 0.489, feature_sparsity = 0.4803, only feature_dim = 10 profile/performance statistics), so bans hide as feature-space in-liers rather than outliers. That is exactly conformity's regime, and its landmarker is shifted hard to the top (mean 0.8111, p50 0.8696) with a compact spread, consistent with a dense template mass the negative-residual signal can rank inside. Pure outlierness is dead here: the density landmarker is degenerate (p50 = p90 = p95 = 0.0, mean 0.0023), so LOF/kNN and one-class boundaries have nothing to separate in a graph with avg_degree 88.28 and density 0.015 where embeddings collapse. attr_struct_mismatch is the strongest genuinely separated tail (p90 0.7175, p95 0.7991, p99 0.9141, std 0.2454) and is the right cross-modal view for this domain: a banned worker's stated profile/performance attributes disagree with the co-task structure they actually sit in. local_affinity is complementary rather than redundant: homophily = 0.7492 means neighbours normally agree, so the low-agreement tail (p95 0.4959, p99 0.6969) marks workers who share tasks with peers they do not resemble. community adds the collusion view: modularity 0.5194 over 26 communities with clustering_coeff 0.5329 means co-task groups are real, and low adherence (p90 0.5439, p99 0.7341) picks up workers spraying across project clusters, a classic ban pattern. I drop homophily_violation as near-duplicate of local_affinity, and drop reconstruction/adversarial/spectral: with feature_dim = 10 and spectral_gap 0.132 on a dense graph, deep reconstruction and high-frequency response mostly re-encode degree (degree_std 161.82, max_degree 2138) rather than misconduct.

Banned tolokers are workers whose behaviour is off but whose profile looks ordinary: with only feature_dim=10 profile/performance statistics and feature_dup_rate=0.489 plus feature_sparsity=0.48, the feature matrix is template-dominated, so banned workers are feature-space in-liers rather than outliers. That is exactly the conformity regime (dup_rate >= 0.4), and its landmarker sits high and left-skewed (mean 0.811, p50 0.870) so the mechanism is present; it is deterministic and cheap, so it leads. attr_struct_mismatch is the natural complement in this domain: the ban decision comes from task behaviour while the graph edges come from co-working on the same tasks, so a worker whose performance attributes disagree with the structural position they occupy is the practitioner's suspicion; it has the widest, most separated upper tail of the landmarkers (std 0.245, p90 0.718, p99 0.914), and it reads across modalities rather than within one. local_affinity adds the neighbour-agreement view that homophily=0.749 licenses: with avg_degree=88 and clustering=0.533, co-working neighbourhoods are dense and coherent, so a worker who disagrees with the peers they share tasks with is a real signal, and its tail (p99 0.697 against mean 0.230) is separated. community covers the coordination angle: modularity=0.519 over 26 communities means the 13 projects induce genuine task clusters, and a banned worker who adheres to none of them (p99 0.734) is caught here and nowhere else. I deliberately drop density (landmarker is degenerate: p50=p90=p95=0.0, mean 0.002, no usable ranking at this density of 0.015), spectral (weakest tail, p95 0.416, and spectral_gap=0.132 with no power-law structure makes high-frequency response mostly a degree artefact on a graph with degree_std=162), homophily_violation (redundant with local_affinity, same homophily premise, same within-modality view), and the heavy learned paradigms (reconstruction, contrastive, adversarial, one_class) whose outlier-in-embedding-space assumption is the opposite of the camouflage-by-conformity regime the feature duplication indicates.
